sources.entry: C: _Crafting Interpreters: A Bytecode Virtual Machine_

summary.title: A Bytecode Virtual Machine
summary.one_liner: Learn why tree-walking interpreters are slow and how to start building a bytecode virtual machine in C from scratch, without relying on host-language runtime features.
takeaways: Tree-walking interpreters like jlox are too slow for general-purpose scripting languages.
A jlox interpreter relies on JVM features such as instanceof and garbage collection that a custom VM must provide itself.
The next step is building a bytecode virtual machine from scratch using only the C standard library.
summary.summary: This page is the opening chapter of Crafting Interpreters' second half, introducing the move from the Java tree-walking interpreter (jlox) to a bytecode virtual machine. It argues that AST walking is too slow for interesting programs and that jlox quietly depends on JVM services like type checks and garbage collection. The chapter sets up the goal of building a VM in C with only the standard library. The excerpt provided is brief, so details of the implementation are not covered here.
